item.title: NCFM: England and Wales, Circumcision, Turning to Child Abuse
item.description: CPS guidance in England and Wales now recognizes that non‑therapeutic circumcision can constitute child abuse when it causes harm. With documented infant deaths, severe injuries, and growing legal scrutiny, NCFM’s Intactivist work—and our support for the Oregon case Mininger et al. v. State of Oregon—has never been more urgent.

item.title: NCFM: The State of Men’s Health Act: A Turning Point in Federal Recognition of a National Crisis
item.description: The State of Men’s Health Act (H.R. 7602) marks the first major federal acknowledgment that American men face a worsening public‑health crisis. With no new funding and decades of advocacy behind it—from the American Urological Association to the Men’s Health Network and the National Coalition for Men—the bill establishes a long‑overdue federal framework to study and address male health disparities

item.title: NCFM Files SUPREME COURT PETITION FOR WRIT OF CERTIORARI in NCFM v. Selective Service System
item.description: The Supreme Court declined NCFM’s earlier draft‑registration case because Congress was already reconsidering the male‑only draft and the Court deferred to the political branches on military affairs. That reform effort collapsed only after Senators Josh Hawley, Tom Cotton, and Marco Rubio threatened to block the 2021 defense bill if women were included in Selective Service—leaving the discriminatory system intact and shaping the Court’s refusal to intervene.
